Definition: An invalid syllogism: a negative premise ('no A is B') combined with another premise cannot yield an affirmative conclusion ('some C is B').
Example: Someone argues, 'No fish are mammals. Some pets are fish, so some pets are mammals.'
FaithDiscussionExample: Someone argues, 'No work earns salvation. Some church activities are works, so some church activities earn salvation' — the form cannot carry that conclusion.
Fallacy: Affirmative Conclusion from a Negative Premise
HowToRespond: Point to the form, not the faith: 'A negative premise can't yield that positive conclusion — let's rebuild the argument.'
